description: Team Titrant unites pharmaceutical sciences, computational modeling, and environmental data analytics to solve agricultural challenges. Rooted in pharmacognosy and precision data science, we bridge orbital Earth observation with on-ground crop quality. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we built PhytoSentinel—transforming live NASA satellite agroclimatology into actionable pre-harvest interventions that safeguard bioactive compounds, prevent spoilage, and protect high-value crops from climate stress.
summary:
We developed PhytoSentinel, a precision pharmacognosy and Earth-observation web dashboard that protects the bioactive potency and shelf life of high-value crops—led by Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)—during the critical pre-harvest window.

Conventional agricultural remote sensing tracks bulk canopy greenness (such as NDVI), which only detects crop stress after visible damage occurs. However, sudden pre-harvest heatwaves and root-zone moisture surges silently degrade heat-sensitive secondary metabolites—including anthocyanins, ellagic acid, and ascorbic acid (Vitamin C)—and trigger rapid fungal spoilage (Botrytis cinerea) 24 to 48 hours before harvest.

PhytoSentinel directly addresses this challenge by connecting to the live NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (T2M, RH2M, and GWETPROF) across major agricultural hubs like Mahabaleshwar, India, and Watsonville, USA. Our risk-assessment engine evaluates live temperature, humidity, and soil moisture against crop-specific pharmacognostic thresholds to calculate a real-time Crop Risk Score (0–100), model phytochemical retention, and recommend targeted interventions such as deploying shade-nets or advancing harvest schedules. By turning orbital telemetry into pre-harvest quality protection, PhytoSentinel prevents silent nutritional loss, reduces post-harvest food waste, and safeguards farmer livelihoods.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

PhytoSentinel is a web-based Earth-observation and pharmacognostic decision-support dashboard that monitors pre-harvest environmental stress in high-value crops, led by Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa).

  1. Automated Satellite Data Ingestion: When a user selects an agricultural region—such as Mahabaleshwar, India (17.9237° N, 73.6586° E) or Watsonville, USA (36.9102° N, -121.7569° E)—the application automatically queries the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (community=AG) to retrieve live daily telemetry for Canopy Temperature (T2M), Relative Humidity (RH2M), and Root-Zone Soil Moisture (GWETPROF).
  2. Pharmacognostic Risk Engine: The telemetry inputs are evaluated against Strawberry's physiological thresholds (15–24°C optimal temperature, 0.22–0.30 m³/m³ soil moisture, < 80% relative humidity). Using multi-factor risk scoring, PhytoSentinel calculates a live 0–100 Crop Risk Index and models real-time retention percentages for key secondary metabolites: Anthocyanins (Pelargonidin-3-glucoside), Ellagic Acid, and Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C).
  3. Actionable Field Guidance & Stress Simulation: Whenever thermal (≥ 28°C) or fungal (soil moisture ≥ 0.34 m³/m³ and humidity ≥ 80%) thresholds are breached, the dashboard triggers immediate agronomic alerts—such as deploying 30% shade-nets, initiating pulsed micro-mist cooling, or advancing harvest by 24–48 hours ahead of Botrytis cinerea (gray mold) outbreaks. An interactive Pre-Harvest Stress Spike simulator also allows growers and researchers to model acute heatwave scenarios.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Preventing Silent Nutritional & Economic Loss: Farmers no longer have to wait for visible leaf wilting or post-harvest rot to discover crop degradation. Early alerts preserve fruit firmness, antioxidant potency, and market grade.
  • Zero-Hardware Accessibility: Because PhytoSentinel relies on open NASA satellite agroclimatology rather than expensive on-farm IoT sensors, smallholder farmers in developing agricultural hubs gain precision-agriculture insights using only a browser.
  • Intended Impact: By reducing pre-harvest phytochemical degradation and fungal spoilage, PhytoSentinel aims to cut post-harvest horticultural waste, stabilize farmer incomes, and protect the nutritional quality of specialty crops worldwide.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Creativity (Pharmacognosy Meets Orbital Telemetry): While traditional agricultural platforms focus solely on bulk biomass or greenness (NDVI), PhytoSentinel introduces biochemical quality protection—connecting NASA microclimate telemetry directly to secondary metabolite stability and post-harvest shelf life.
    • Biological Specificity: Different crops degrade under distinct stress thresholds; our architecture supports customizable crop profiles (including Ashwagandha, Mentha, and Soybean alongside Strawberry).
    • Actionability Over Raw Data: Raw meteorological numbers are difficult for growers to interpret, so we translated API outputs into a clear 0–100 score and concrete field actions.
    • Low-Latency & Offline Resilience: We included interactive parameter sliders and stress simulation controls alongside live NASA API syncing so users can test scenarios even under low-connectivity field conditions.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • NASA Data & APIs: NASA POWER Temporal Daily Point Agroclimatology API (T2M, RH2M, GWETPROF), informed by thermal and soil-moisture remote sensing concepts from ISS ECOSTRESS and NASA SMAP.
  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES6+), React, HTML5, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Development & Deployment Software: Vite, Lovable, GitHub (version control), VSCodium on Linux Mint, and Vercel (cloud hosting and continuous deployment).
